As indicated in the survey conducted by the Crow Tribe's Office of Coal Research, the Crow People are very apprehensive of the anticipated changes, feel ill-informed of both the possibilities and probabilities of the many aspects of coal development, (particularly those of a socio-economic nature), and feel that they have far too little influence over future development.
In order to correct this existing socio-political impact and to assist the Tribe to avoid, modify, or accomodate for future socio-economic impacts, a detailed study and planning program is needed.

These studies must be tailored to the peculiarities of the Crow situation and must delve far deeper than previous analyses. Planning must be an on-going process. It is a basic responsibility of the Crow Tribe and will require the assistance and resources of all appropriate municipal, state and federal organizations as well as the various coal companies.

A modest beginning in fulfilling this responsibility has been made through the Crow Tribe's Office of Coal Research. Every effort needs to be made to give the Tribe the needed assistance and cooperation in order to insure maximum effectiveness in their planning process.
Inter-Scenario Comparisons
The discussion to this point has focused primarily on what is considered to be Westmoreland Resources' most probable level of development (Scenario 1). The analysis based on this level has investigated a number of variables, most notably the labor force participation rate and the presence or absence of other significant Crow coal production.
